title: SSL/TLS: certificates, certificate authorities and validity

videos.script: Lesson 5 encrypted a connection. Encryption alone only proves you are talking privately to somebody. It does not prove who. {{who}} A certificate is how a server proves it is the one its name says. It is signed by an authority your computer already trusts, and it is checked on every connection, in milliseconds, without anybody seeing it. {{cert}} Most days that check is invisible. When it fails, it fails loudly: a red page in the browser, an error in a program, a printer that stops sending scans. It fails for a handful of reasons, and each has its own message. {{fail}} In this lesson you will read a certificate field by field and follow the chain that makes it trustworthy. You will look at the store of authorities your machine trusts. {{steps}} Then you will break it four ways, on purpose, and see what each failure says. You will install your office's own authority, and learn to see an expiry coming before it arrives. {{more}}
